benchmarks.note: three sample vehicles, parts + labor (2017 F-150 $933, 2019 BMW 740i $2,309, 2017 Civic $4,414); says OEM converters run about $800-$3,000, aftermarket $200-$800, typical book time one to three hours; updated 2026-09-03

benchmarks.name: AAA
benchmarks.note: parts + labor; parts alone $300-$2,500; examples Honda $1,000-$2,200, Ford $950-$2,700, BMW $1,450-$4,000; no publish date shown

finding: The live range of $480-$2,450 is too low at the bottom and a little low at the top. Built totals per converter (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2014 Kia Soul 1.6L about $1,117-$1,862 (0.9-1.4 hr); midsize 2011 Chevrolet Equinox 2.4L about $634-$2,255 (1.3-2.6 hr); truck 2016 F-150 5.0L about $824-$1,697 (0.9-2.3 hr); luxury 2008 Acura RDX about $956-$2,778 (1.3-1.8 hr). With a CARB-compliant aftermarket part instead: F-150 about $2,576-$2,836, RDX about $2,583-$2,715; no CARB aftermarket part was found for the Soul or the Equinox. So the lowest total we can build is about $634, using the cheapest federal-only aftermarket converter on the Equinox; the other classes start at $824-$1,117. $480 is below anything found. Labor is the small part of this job (0.9-2.6 hours, about $110-$420); the converter itself decides the price. At the top, genuine parts reach about $2,255 on the Equinox and about $2,780 on the RDX, CARB parts reach about $2,840 on the truck, and outside benchmarks run higher still (RepairPal average $2,293-$2,468, AAA $1,000-$4,000, ConsumerAffairs samples $933-$4,414). Roughly $650-$2,300 for most federal-emissions vehicles and up to about $2,850 with genuine parts on some vehicles or in CARB states fits the evidence. How solid the labor times are: seven of the eight figures are manufacturer times for the example model. Midsize is GM's own special-coverage time for the 2010-2011 Equinox 2.4L (1.3 hr front-wheel drive, 2.6 hr all-wheel drive). Luxury is Acura's own warranty time for the 2007-10 RDX warm-up converter (1.3 hr 2WD, 1.8 hr SH-AWD). Truck is Ford's own time for the F-150 5.0L, but for the 2022-2023 model years rather than 2016 (0.9 hr left, 2.3 hr right). Economy pairs Kia's recall time for the 2012-2016 Soul 1.6L (1.4 hr, which includes a 0.3 hr software update) with a Honda warranty time for a CR-Z (0.9 hr), which is not a Soul. All are manufacturer warranty or recall times on clean vehicles, the short end of what shops bill; rusted or seized exhaust hardware takes longer. Other caveats: the GM coverage notice as recorded does not say which of the Equinox's two converters it replaces, so the parts range spans the cheapest aftermarket converter to the dearest genuine one; the Soul has one priced aftermarket listing; the RDX CARB listing does not state its position and was backordered; these examples (2008-2014 model years) are older than the truck example. An earlier version of this check used a Toyota Corolla, Toyota Camry and BMW 328i, for which no manufacturer labor time could be found; the examples were changed to vehicles whose makers publish one.
extras: Quotes often add oxygen or air-fuel sensors (frequently replaced or seized during removal), new gaskets, studs, nuts and clamps, a diagnosis fee for the catalyst-efficiency code, shop supplies and sales tax. Vehicles with two or more converters may need more than one. In California and other CARB states only CARB-compliant or OEM converters are legal, which can double the parts price; federal-only parts cannot be installed there. A converter usually fails for a reason (misfire, oil or coolant burning), so repairs to the root cause may be quoted too. A failed original converter may still be covered by the federal emissions warranty (8 years / 80,000 miles), and theft replacement may be an insurance claim.
